item.text: The failed test run was a sequencing artifact from running `javac` and `java` in parallel against the same files. I’m rerunning compile first, then executing the tests and demo sequentially.

I further refactored the codebase into a cleaner library/demo/test split. [TwoPointers.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/002_two_pointers_technique/TwoPointers.java:1) is now a pure utility API with `findPairWithSum(...)` returning an `Optional<PairMatch>` and `hasPairWithSum(...)` kept as the simple boolean wrapper. That removes the earlier mixing of algorithm logic with console execution and makes the code reusable. I also fixed an implementation bug by comparing sums as `long`, so extreme `int` inputs no longer overflow and produce false results.

I moved the example runner into [TwoPointersDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/002_two_pointers_technique/TwoPointersDemo.java:1) and added a small executable regression harness in [TwoPointersTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/002_two_pointers_technique/TwoPointersTest.java:1). The tests cover a normal match, no-match behavior, unsorted-input rejection, and overflow safety.

Verification: `javac TwoPointers.java TwoPointersDemo.java TwoPointersTest.java` succeeded, `java TwoPointersTest` passed with no output, and `java TwoPointersDemo` printed `Optional[PairMatch[leftIndex=0, rightIndex=3, leftValue=-3, rightValue=1]]`.
